newsitem.title: FRANCE: Tax energy to protect welfare state, Euro-MPs say.
newsitem.headline: Tax energy to protect welfare state, Euro-MPs say.

text.p: European Union governments should reduce the burden of social security systems on businesses and employees by cutting tax on labour and taxing CO2 instead, the European Parliament said on Wednesday.
The European Parliament adopted a report from its employment and social affairs committee which warns that national social security schemes are under great strain.
Euro-MPs said member states should diversify their sources of financing for the welfare state, such as by taxing factors "such as environmentally damaging energy consumption".

The report, drafted in response to the European Commission's communication on the future of social protection, COM(95)466, and a related report, COM(95)457, said the EU should be more active in ensuring its member states respect their EU treaty commitment to provide "a high level of...social protection.
Creating more jobs and increasing the numbers of contributors would be the best way of stabilising social security schemes, Euro-MPs said.
But they rejected workfare, "forced labour", as a condition for entitlement to benefit.
